chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad who said:

I wrote to Al-Akheir (peace be upon him): A man died and upon him was a debt of making up fasts from the month of Ramadan for ten days, and he has two guardians. Is it permissible for both of them to make it up for him together, five days by one of the two guardians and five days by the other?
So he (peace be upon him) signed: The elder of his guardians should make it up for him, ten days, by guardianship, if Allah wills.

key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: Making up missed obligatory acts, specifically fasting
key_terms.وِلَاءً: By guardianship / through the authority of a guardian

ai.seo_question: Can two guardians split the making up of missed fasts for a deceased person?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of vicarious fasting (qadā’ al-ṣawm) for a deceased person, specifically addressing whether multiple heirs can split the obligation or if it must be consolidated. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the elder guardian performs all ten days through a single act of guardianship (wilā’), establishing the principle that the obligation is discharged by the representative rather than being fragmented among heirs. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the spiritual debt of fasting is satisfied by the representative's action, ensuring the deceased's obligation is fully cleared without requiring proportional division.
